scope: Each planned claim was read against its cited lines and then traced through the code that controls the result: callers, templates, configuration, schema scripts, workflows and tests. Only files inside the Target were opened. The auditor had no writer notes and did not build or run the application.

anchor: There was an error in creating the owner.

claim: The demo route /oups throws on any unauthenticated GET and is linked from the main menu

claim: Edit an owner: flow and messages as written; an unknown id returns the error page with the message Owner not found with id:
limitation: Steps 1 to 4 are supported. The failure line overstates: the controller throws IllegalArgumentException with that text, but error.html:18 only renders the message attribute, the main configuration never enables error message inclusion, and only CrashControllerIntegrationTests.java:51 sets spring.web.error.include-message=ALWAYS. Spring Boot's default is not to include it, so the error page shows no message text by default (framework default is outside the repository). Correct to say an error page is returned and the message appears only if inclusion is enabled

claim: Add a pet: duplicate-name and future-date rejection, saveAndFlush, unique-name violation handling, success message; MySQL caveat

claim: Book a visit: new Visit dated tomorrow, date must be after today, saved, success message; an unknown owner or pet raises IllegalArgumentException and the error page shows the message
limitation: Steps 1 to 3 are supported. Correct to JSON, or mark XML Inferred. No-expiry is read from a MutableConfiguration with only statistics set, a default of the JCache provider, not shown in source

claim: Trigger the demo error page: menu links /oups, triggerException throws RuntimeException rendered with the error template, by design, a test asserts the behavior
